setup: Kneel on a pad, knees hip-width
Tuck your toes or point them back
Body straight from knees to head
execution: Lean back slowly as one straight line
Go only as far as you can control
Pull yourself back up with your thighs
Keep your hips straight the whole time

notes: Use a thick pad under the knees.
Start with a small lean and increase the range over weeks; the front of the thigh is very stretched at the bottom.
Have a way back up: a band anchored in front to hold, or hands ready to catch on the floor behind.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain at the knee or front of the thigh that builds
Pain that changes how you move

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at floor level, figure kneeling facing right. Shows the straight line from knees to head and how far the body leans back.

keyPositions.label: Kneeling
keyPositions.describe: Kneeling upright on a pad, knees hip-width, shins flat on the floor. Body in a straight line from knees to head. Arms crossed on the chest or held forward.

keyPositions.label: Lean back
keyPositions.describe: Body leaning back as one straight line from knees to head, hips still straight. Knees more bent. The lean is moderate, not lying back.

ikHints: Knees and shins fixed on the pad
Hip angle stays straight in every frame
emphasise: Straight line from knees to head
